subject.title: fix(agents): pass attemptNumber instead of apiKeyIndex to retry callbacks (#102938)

question: Should the provider plugin callback permanently expose `attempt`, `apiKeyIndex`, and `attemptNumber`, and if so should `attempt` remain a supported alias or enter a defined deprecation/removal path?
rationale: The helper is exported through the shipped plugin SDK, and source inspection cannot determine the intended long-term public contract or removal policy.

options.title: Keep a permanent alias
options.body: Add the two explicit fields but retain `attempt` as a documented, non-deprecated alias for `apiKeyIndex`, minimizing upgrade uncertainty.

options.title: Approve deprecation
options.body: Keep the proposed deprecation only with a maintainer-approved compatibility period, removal plan, and plugin-facing documentation.

options.title: Avoid API expansion
options.body: Leave the public callback unchanged and decline custom per-key retry-counter support until a broader retry-event contract is designed.

recommendation.title: Keep a permanent alias
recommendation.body: Add the two explicit fields but retain `attempt` as a documented, non-deprecated alias for `apiKeyIndex`, minimizing upgrade uncertainty.

likelyOwner.reason: The behavior and public helper appear to originate in their provider rotation work, with subsequent maintenance in the same authentication surface.
